# Lazypock

> Self-hosted backend-as-a-service in Rust + Postgres. One binary — API, auth, realtime, jobs, hooks and the Studio — over real Postgres tables with RLS permissions, and a PocketBase-canonical REST API so existing PocketBase clients and SDKs work unchanged.

This file is for AI assistants and crawlers. The most useful page for generating a file that can be
imported into a Lazypock server (Studio → Settings → Import / Backups, or `POST /api/import`) is the
backup format reference below.

## API shape

Records live at `/api/collections/{collection}/records(/{id})` and use the PocketBase list envelope
(`page`, `perPage`, `totalItems`, `totalPages`, `items`). Auth is at
`/api/collections/{collection}/auth-with-password`, `auth-refresh`, `auth-with-oauth2`,
`auth-methods`, `request-verification`, `request-password-reset` and their `confirm-*` pairs. Files
are served from `/api/files/{collection}/{record}/{filename}` (also `?preset=`, `?thumb=`,
`/thumbs/{size}`, `/scale/{size}`, and by file id at `/api/files/{id}`). Realtime is **SSE** at
`/api/realtime`, resumable with `Last-Event-ID`. `POST /api/batch` is all-or-nothing in one
transaction, and `/api/jwks` publishes the access-token keys.

## Import / backup JSON format

- [Backup & import JSON format](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/backup): envelope, collections, fields, types, rules, indexes, records, examples, PocketBase 23+ compatibility, and the NDJSON zip archive used for large databases.
- [JSON Schema (backup.schema.json)](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/backup.schema.json): machine-readable contract for the canonical `{ "collections": [...] }` payload.

Endpoints: `GET /api/export` (download JSON), `GET /api/export/archive` (download a streamed NDJSON
zip for large databases), `POST /api/import` (restore JSON or a multipart archive, superuser only),
`GET /api/import/preflight` (whether automatic undo is available), `GET /api/import/status`, and
`POST /api/import/rollback`. An import never deletes a collection unless `deleteMissing` asks, and
never writes a `_`-prefixed system collection.

An archive contains `manifest.json`, `schema.json`, `data/<collection>.ndjson`, `files.ndjson` and
`files/<storage_path>` (the uploaded blobs). The Studio previews an archive by reading only
`manifest.json` from the browser before uploading it.

## Docs

- [What is Lazypock](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/): overview and feature list.
- [Architecture](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/architecture): system layers, request lifecycle, realtime.
- [Server guide](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/server): Docker, binary, first-time setup, filters, production, env vars.
- [TypeScript SDK](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/sdk/typescript): install, codegen, queries, realtime, files, auth.
- [All SDKs](https://lazypock.gnuzd.dev/sdk): TypeScript (Swift, Android, Godot marked coming soon).
